title: The Messaging Mistake Everyone Makes on LinkedIn (And How to Fix It in Two Sentences)
summary: Toby Blatchford-Tagg runs The Lead Lab, a UK agency that manages more than a thousand LinkedIn profiles for clients after rebuilding the company out of a 40-seat B2B telemarketing operation. His argument is that outbound did not die with cold calling; the cost of a conversation moved, and LinkedIn now produces a lead for roughly 40% less than email in nearly every sector he works in. The tactical core of the episode is the messaging fix: cleanse 30% of any Sales Navigator list before you send, never sell in the connection request, and write the first two sentences as a benefit to the reader in the tone of a chat rather than a memo, because formality itself is what makes replying feel like work. Anyone running LinkedIn outreach, rebuilding an outbound motion, or deciding where AI actually belongs in a sales stack will get something concrete out of it.
keyQuote: The more formal you are, the more of a hassle it is to reply. So the more relaxed you are in your outgoing, the more relaxed they can be in their response.
guestBio: Toby Blatchford-Tagg is Group CEO of The Lead Lab, a B2B outreach agency based in Exeter in the UK. He started the business roughly eighteen years ago as a cold-calling telemarketing agency, running around 40 seats selling everything from part-time CFOs to office coffee. He also built and later sold a B2C telemarketing company, having decided that consumer cold calling had no long-term future. When COVID wiped out most of the client base overnight, he rebuilt the company around LinkedIn automation, a channel he had been working by hand for his own pipeline for years. The Lead Lab now manages over a thousand LinkedIn profiles, handling data, copywriting, and response management for clients from two-person startups up to enterprise teams, with more customers in the US than the UK.
